content: Patients initiating therapy for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection or those who have experienced relapse after prior pegylated interferon (PEG) and ribavirin (RBV) therapy should follow specific treatment guidelines based on HCV genotype, as outlined by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) and the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) in April 2014. Peginterferon is not recommended as monotherapy for any patient group. For melanoma patients with microscopic or gross nodal involvement, peginterferon alfa-2b is indicated within 84 days of definitive surgical resection, including complete lymphadenectomy. The recommended dosing is 6 mcg/kg subcutaneously weekly for 8 doses, followed by 3 mcg/kg weekly for up to 5 years. Dose reductions of 25% and 50% are recommended for patients with moderate and severe renal impairment, respectively. For patients with creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 30–50 mL/min, a 25% dose reduction is advised, while for those with CrCl of 10–29 mL/min (including hemodialysis), a 50% reduction is recommended. The pharmacokinetics of peginterferon alfa-2b at these doses in melanoma patients with varying degrees of renal impairment have not been studied. Peginterferon alfa-2b has not been studied in melanoma patients with hepatic impairment. In patients treated for viral hepatitis, peginterferon alfa-2b is contraindicated in those with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh scores >6). If hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh scores >6) occurs during treatment, Sylatron (peginterferon alfa-2b) should be discontinued. For thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis, the safety and efficacy of peginterferon alfa-2b have not been established in patients under 3 years of age. For patients aged 3–17 years, the recommended dose is 60 mcg/m² subcutaneously weekly, in combination with ribavirin at 15 mg/kg/day orally in divided doses every 12 hours, administered on the same day each week. Peginterferon alfa-2b can increase the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, and coadministration is contraindicated. Fezolinetant's area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration are increased when coadministered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, including peginterferon alfa-2b. This interaction may increase toxicity, and alternative drugs should be considered. Peginterferon alfa-2b and deferiprone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Coadministration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If deferiprone must be used with other drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis, absolute neutrophil count should be monitored more frequently. Peginterferon alfa-2b and pexidartinib both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Coadministration of pexidartinib with other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. Similarly, peginterferon alfa-2b and pretomanid may increase each other's toxicity, particularly hepatotoxicity. Alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements, should be avoided during pretomanid therapy. Coadministration of peginterferon alfa-2b with acalabrutinib may increase the risk of myelosuppressive effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Peginterferon alfa-2b may also enhance the adverse effects of aldesleukin, including myocardial and renal toxicity, through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. When peginterferon alfa-2b is coadministered with drugs metabolized by CYP2D6, such as amitriptyline, amoxapine, aripiprazole, atomoxetine, chlorpromazine, clomipramine, codeine, desipramine, dextromethorphan, doxepin, duloxetine, fluoxetine, haloperidol, imipramine, maprotiline, methamphetamine, metoprolol, mexiletine, mirtazapine, nortriptyline, palonosetron, or paroxetine, the therapeutic effects of these drugs may be altered. Peginterferon alfa-2b may increase or decrease the levels of these CYP2D6 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases the levels of drugs metabolized by CYP2C9/10, such as bosentan, celecoxib, dapsone, diclofenac, etravirine, fluvastatin, glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, ibuprofen, ibuprofen IV, indomethacin, losartan, montelukast, naproxen, and nateglinide. The therapeutic effects of these drugs may be altered, and caution and monitoring are recommended. Methadone levels may be elevated when coadministered with peginterferon alfa-2b, increasing pharmacologic effects and adverse reactions. Patients should be monitored for signs of increased narcotic effects, and methadone doses should be adjusted as needed. Ifosfamide and peginterferon alfa-2b may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly enhancing myelosuppressive effects. Monitoring for increased risk of myelosuppression is advised. Coadministration of peginterferon alfa-2b with lamivudine may increase the risk of liver decompensation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. In summary, peginterferon alfa-2b interacts with a wide range of drugs, primarily through effects on hepatic enzyme metabolism (CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP2C9/10). These interactions may alter drug levels, therapeutic effects, and toxicity profiles. Caution, monitoring, and dose adjustments are often necessary to mitigate risks.
